*   **Ordering Provider:** Dr. [First Name] Duval, MD, [Clinic Name]

Dear Member Appeals Department,

I am writing to formally appeal MVP Health Care’s denial of the prior authorization request submitted by my provider, Dr. Duval, for a knee arthroscopy with medial meniscectomy (CPT 29881). The denial notice dated 2026-08-13 states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." 

This determination is clinically incorrect and directly contradicts my medical records, which demonstrate that I have not only satisfied but significantly exceeded the non-operative treatment thresholds outlined in MVP's governing medical criteria, **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1764 for Knee Arthroscopy** (formerly National Imaging Associates, Inc. Clinical Guideline 316). 

Below, I map my clinical records directly to your policy requirements to demonstrate full medical necessity.

### 1. Documented Conservative Treatment Far Exceeds the Policy's 6-Week Trial Requirement
According to the governing policy, most meniscal tears require documentation of:
> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least TWO of the following:"
> *   "Rest or activity modifications/limitations"
> *   "Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol"
> *   "Physical therapy modalities"
> *   "Injections: corticosteroid, NSAID, viscosupplementation"

My medical history documents **over 12 months** of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest and physical limitations, including a multi-modal trial of conservative treatments that far exceeds the required 6-week timeframe:
*   **Supervised Physical Therapy (Satisfies "Physical therapy modalities"):** I participated in a formal, supervised physical therapy program focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion for **14 weeks** (from 2026-04-08 to 2026-07-15), completing **24 visits**. This is fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Pharmacologic Treatment (Satisfies "Pharmacologic treatment..."):** I have taken prescribed oral NSAIDs daily for **8 months** without adequate pain relief.
*   **Joint Injections (Satisfies "Injections..."):** I received a diagnostic and therapeutic intra-articular corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-10, which provided only 4 weeks of partial, temporary relief. 

### 2. Clinical Exception: Conservative Care is Not Required Due to a Mechanically Locked Knee
Furthermore, even if my 14 weeks of physical therapy and 8 months of NSAIDs were not documented (which they are), your policy explicitly waives the non-operative treatment requirement for patients presenting with an acutely locked knee and a bucket-handle tear. 

Your policy states that meniscectomy is indicated without conservative care if:
> "There has been the acute onset of locking (does not include catching, popping, cracking, etc.); AND There is MRI evidence of a bucket-handle or displaced meniscal fragment that correlates with the correct compartment (i.e., medial tenderness and locking, for a medial meniscus tear)"

My clinical presentation fits this emergency exception perfectly:
*   **Mechanical Symptoms:** I suffer from mechanical "locking" and "giving way" of the knee, making it impossible to kneel or squat and limiting me strictly to level walking. My range of motion is severely limited by pain.
*   **MRI Evidence:** A standing knee MRI performed on 2026-07-02 confirmed a **displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus** with mechanical locking. 
*   **Anatomical Correlation:** My physical examination demonstrates positive provocative meniscal testing on the affected side, directly correlating with the medial compartment locking and tenderness.

### 3. Fulfillment of All Other General Policy Requirements
Additionally, I satisfy all other clinical requirements mandated by Evolent Clinical Guideline 1764:
*   **Preserved Joint Space (Kellgren-Lawrence Grading):** My standing imaging from 2026-07-02 confirms my articular cartilage is well preserved, grading as a **Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 1**. This satisfies the policy requirement of having "no more than K-L 2 changes" (moderate/severe osteoarthritis is absent).
*   **Cortisone Injection Timing:** My last corticosteroid injection was on 2026-05-10. This is well outside the policy’s exclusion period, satisfying the requirement of "No intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery".
*   **Overall Health Status:** I am medically optimized for surgery. I have no active local or systemic infections, no untreated substance use or drug dependencies, a stable BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

### Conclusion
I have a severe, structural, mechanically locking injury (displaced bucket-handle medial meniscus tear) that cannot heal on its own and has failed to improve after 14 weeks of physical therapy and 8 months of medication. Denying this minimally invasive arthroscopic procedure forces me to live in chronic pain with limited mobility, risking further joint damage.

Based on the overwhelming clinical documentation attached, I request that you immediately reverse this denial and approve the requested knee arthroscopy with medial meniscectomy (CPT 29881). 

Thank you for your prompt review of this appeal. Please contact me or Dr. Duval’s office at [Provider Phone Number] if any further clinical documentation is required.

Sincerely,

Cameron Brooks
Member ID: W412154328
[Patient Signature]
